title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 194
paragraphs: It happened that fifteen of these ships put out to sea considerably later than the rest, and they caught sight of the Greek ships at Artemisium. The barbarians assumed these were their own vessels and sailed toward them, only to fall among the enemy. Their commander was Sandokes son of Thamasios, governor of Kyme in Aiolia, whom King Darius had once taken and crucified (he being one of the Royal Judges) for this reason: Sandokes had delivered an unjust verdict for money. After he had been hung up, Darius reconsidered and found that his services to the royal house outweighed his offenses; realizing this, and seeing that he had acted more hastily than wisely, Darius let him go. So he escaped from King Darius and survived; but now, sailing in toward the Greeks, he was not destined to escape a second time. For when the Greeks saw them sailing up, they perceived the mistake, put out against them, and captured them without difficulty.
